This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed
investing to full-service wealth management all in one place. No matter your investing
goal, life stage, amount to invest or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman. Ukraine continues to insist that its access to Elon
Musk's Starlink Internet Service was deliberately cut off briefly earlier this week. The military
version of Starlink is used in Ukraine's targeting systems. Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke
with reporters Saturday and said whatever happened was not deliberate.
No one at the White House ordered anyone to slow down internet or slow down speed so that
certain drones couldn't use it. But my understanding is it's back up and running. That's what I
read. That's what we heard two days ago. Ukraine's president says his military officers
were informed by their U.S. counterparts that there would be consequences if they did not
stop attacking Russian oil facilities. Hundreds of people gathered for a No Kings protest
in Tulsa, Oklahoma Saturday. They were urging citizens to vote in November's midterm elections.
KWGS's Tegan Smith has more on the voters' concerns.
People chanted after lining the streets of Tulsa with signs and instruments. Tulsa's local chapter
of the National Grassroots Movement in Divisible organized Saturday's No Kings protest.
The focus of this particular protest is encouraging citizens to vote this November. 21-year-old
Alex Wade says the Republican supermajority in Oklahoma has gone on too long and hopes
for change going forward.
We've got to flip the state. They've had the state for my entire life, and I've never
seen a single good thing that the right side has done.
Early voting in Oklahoma begins October 28th. For NPR News, I'm Tegan Smith in Tulsa.
High fuel prices continue to put the squeeze on family budgets. As Americans prepare for
holiday shopping and travel, GasBuddy estimates that Americans have spent about $82 billion
more on gasoline since March 1st than during the same period last year. M.Piers Winslow
Johnston has our reports.
Petroleum analyst Patrick Dahan says at this point the pressure has extended beyond the
gas pump. He says diesel costs are working their way through the supply chain.
I would like to say that the U.S. economy, the engine, is powered by diesel.
Dahan says heavy, bulky goods and perishable foods are especially exposed, including turkeys
heading to grocery stores for Thanksgiving. Holiday travelers also face higher fuel costs
whether they drive or fly. There's no way to book now and beat it. You can't avoid the
increase in fuel when what comes out of a barrel is fueling the entire U.S. economy.
He says relief depends on what happens next in the conflicts overseas that continue to
disrupt oil supplies.
Winslow Johnston, NPR News. Police in Paris used tear gas and water cannons to disperse
a crowd of protesters who were throwing fireworks, paving stones and other objects on Saturday.
They were part of a larger, more peaceful group protesting poor school conditions and
the rising cost of living. Police say the violent protesters were targeting public buildings,
including city halls and police stations. Protests have been taking place across France
for weeks.
You're listening to NPR News.
Deadlines for registering to vote for the midterm elections are coming up soon in some
states. NPR's Hansi Lo Wang has this rundown of the latest deadlines.
One day, October 19th, is the last chance for eligible voters to register or update
their registration in Alabama, Pennsylvania and South Dakota. The next major voter registration
deadline is on Saturday, October 24th, in Massachusetts and New York. And then October
31st, Halloween, is the last day in North Carolina for signing up in person at the state's
early voting sites. The only state where voter registration is not required is North Dakota.
And many states allow for same-day registration at the polls on November 3rd's election day.
If you're already registered in a state with an earlier deadline, election officials recommend
going to your state's official election website to confirm your status and contact information
before voter registration ends. Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
The Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians Saturday, 7-3, to even the best of seven American
League Championship Series at 2-2. Game 5 is Sunday in Cleveland. Gabby Williams finished
with 26 points, including two go-ahead free throws with less than two minutes left as
Golden State beat the Atlanta Dream Saturday, 68-64. It was the game 1 in the best of seven
WNBA Championship Series. Game 2 takes place Monday night in San Francisco.
There were some upsets at the top of college football on Saturday as No. 1 Georgia fell
to Auburn, 27-24. No. 2 Notre Dame lost to BYU, 28-24. No. 3 Miami beat Florida State,
33-35, and No. 4 Ohio State slipped past defending champion Indiana 19-15. Alabama lost to Tennessee.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

More at WallaceFoundation.org.
